reason: Wording stands, and on better evidence than the verifier had. Internet Archive full-text search returns the scanned 1997 Penguin Poems, Protest, and a Dream itself (poemsprotestandd00juan) and the 1982 Lime Rock A Woman of Genius (womanofgeniusi00juan), both reading: ‘because my hair grew quickly and I learned slowly — and in fact I did cut it in punishment for such stupidity: for there seemed to me no cause for a head to be adorned with hair and naked of learning — which was the more desired embellishment’. So the words, the colon and the dash are Peden’s in the named edition, and the note is right that the excerpt begins mid sentence with a lower-case ‘and’ after a dash; the capital is the card’s. The Arenal and Powell version (‘Then I cut my hair right off to punish my dull-wittedness’) and others word it differently, so there is no drift. Page 15 I could not see (the scan is lending-locked); it rests on the Metanexus citation alone, and is plausible for a facing-page edition with English on the rectos. One correction: the named edition titles the work ‘Response to the Most Illustrious Poetess Sor Filotea de la Cruz’ (confirmed in the scan’s contents and running head), not ‘Reply’; ‘Reply to Sor Philothea’ is the Trueblood convention. A source line citing Peden’s page should use Peden’s title. Also trim the last sentence of the note (‘The source now cites the edition whose page is given’): it is process talk, not something for a card. For the editor: the card’s ‘it’ has no antecedent until ‘hair’ arrives ten words later, and a line about punishing oneself for stupidity is a judgement call at six in the morning. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, person unused, not banned. Correspondence is the right tag: the Respuesta is a letter. Source line 130 characters (133 corrected), leads with the name, no dash; the dash inside the quotation is the translator’s.
